title: Evacuation rehearsal: active→passive choreography, KV sanification, and backup fidelity gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Validate an orchestrated active→passive evacuation (partial and full) that preserves SLO commitments via automated circuit-breaker engagement, progressive load-shedding, and explicit backup-fidelity gates. This ticket coordinates the rehearsal, the backup/restore integrity checks, and post-dr validation metrics. Scope: - One planned full-region evacuation drill (primary -> passive region) with staged traffic siphon and two progressive partial evacuations. - Backup validation: snapshot + WAL checksum verification, incremental rehydrate test to passive region, and KV-store sanification for tombstones/versions. - SLO gates: pre-evacuation acceptance for latency and error budgets; mid-evacuation circuit-breaker thresholds that trigger additional shedding or rollback; post-evacuation steady-state SLO verification. Out-of-scope: cluster-level hardware failovers and long-term runbook rewrites (will be separate follow-ups). Success criteria: 1) Passive region takes ≥95% of traffic for the targeted services within target window without violating P99 latency SLO by >15% sustained over 10 minutes. 2) Snapshot+WAL restores produce bitwise-consistent KV checksums with production sample of keys. 3) Circuit-breaker and load-shed automation engaged and recovered without manual intervention in ≥90% of rehearsals. 4) Runbook steps executed without manual overrides and documented takedowns recorded in the incident log.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-flight: backups verified and checksums recorded (sha256) for last 24h snapshots
Traffic siphon: progressive 25% steps with automated gating; each step verified by canary telemetry
Data fidelity: restored passive KV-store passes spot-checks and sample queries (key space coverage >= 1%)
SLO: no sustained P99 latency degradation >15% beyond baseline for more than 10 minutes after final cutover
Automation: circuit-breaker engages at configured error-rate threshold and triggers load-shedding policy without manual escalation
runbook_steps: Pre-flight (T-48h): snapshot retention confirmation; run backup integrity job and commit checksum artifacts to S3 (s3://redwood-dr/ENG-90532) and link in ticket
Pre-flight (T-1h): open communication channel (#dr-evacuation), throttle non-critical batch jobs, set maintenance windows on ingesters
Step 0: Activate rehearsal mode in Console; disable auto-scaling expansions to avoid noise
Step 1: Canary replay to passive region using production replay harness (replay-job-2026-ENG-90532); verify response signatures for 3 consecutive canary runs
Step 2: Progressive siphon 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 95% using weighted routing; validate health and SLOs at each step
Step 3: Engage KV sanification routines once passive receives write traffic: tombstone reconciliation and version compaction; monitor for conflicts and backfill lag
Step 4: Full snapshot+WAL restore verification: compute sha256 checksums and compare to pre-flight artifacts; record mismatches and abort if >0.1% of sampled keys differ
Step 5: Run smoke tests and alerting sanity (end-to-end flows) then mark passive as primary for the rehearsal window
Step 6: Controlled rollback: revert routing weights in reverse order and validate state convergence; in the event of incomplete convergence, follow rollback_plan
test_plan: Backup integrity job: run snapshot3x+WAL replay against isolated test cluster and assert checksum parity
Failure injection: simulate partial KV write-loss and verify circuit-breaker trips and load-shedding policies enact fallbacks
Latency regression test: run synthetic P99 latency probe for 20 minutes around each siphon step
Rehydration timing: measure time-to-consistency (TTConsistency) for passive after replay; target < 10 minutes for critical key prefixes
Chaos run: small-scale node kill in passive region while passive is serving 50% traffic to validate graceful degradation
rollback_plan: If any acceptance criteria fail at a gating point, immediately revert routing weights to pre-dr baseline, mark the passive region as read-only, and run a diagnostic sweep: 1) Inspect KV conflict logs and WAL replay errors, 2) Restore from last-known-good snapshot into an isolated verification cluster, 3) Notify on-call SRE and PM, 4) If rollback fails, escalate to SEV and follow SEV incident playbook. Document root cause and schedule post-mortem within 48 hours.
decision_log: Decision: use snapshot + WAL incremental replay vs cross-region continuous replication. Rationale: faster validation loop, deterministic checksums, lower operational blast radius for rehearsals.
Decision: gating threshold for circuit-breaker set to 5% error increase over 5m or absolute 2xx->5xx spike >100 req/min — chosen to balance sensitivity and false positives
Decision: enforce sample-keyspace verification (1% of keys) rather than full KV diff due to size; schedule nightly full diffs in off-hours
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: sample-based checksum misses low-frequency corruption; mitigated by nightly full-diff and targeted audits
Tradeoff: faster cutover windows vs increased temporary write-latency due to cross-region writes; we accept transient latency within SLO gates
Risk: automated rollback may not catch subtle semantic divergences in model-serving outputs; require manual QA signoff for model-sensitive routes
